title: Counit comparison for a flat complex on a base open
statement: Let $B,A$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $g:A\to B$ a morphism and $a\in A$. Let $S\subset B$ and $V\subset A$ be opens with $g(a)\in S$, $a\in V$ and $V\subset g^{-1}(S)$, and put $j=g|_V:V\to S$. Let $K$ be a bounded-above complex of flat $\mathcal O_S$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $R=\mathcal O_{B,g(a)}$, $T=\mathcal O_{A,a}$, $x_S=(g(a),g(a)\in S)$, $x_V=(a,a\in V)$, $P=K_{x_S}$ with scalars transported along the inverse $\mathcal O_{S,x_S}\simeq R$, and let $F$ be the stalk functor at $x_V$ followed by scalar restriction along the inverse $\mathcal O_{V,x_V}\simeq T$. Let $LF:D(R)\to D(T)$ and $\varepsilon:LF\circ Q_h\to Q_h\circ\operatorname{extendScalars}(g_a)$ be any universal left-derived pair for extension along the stalk map $g_a:R\to T$. For each $n\in\mathbf Z$ there are $T$-linear isomorphisms $l:F(H^n(Lj^*(Q_h(K))))\simeq H^n(LF(Q_h(P)))$ and $r:H^n(Q_h(\operatorname{extendScalars}(g_a)(P)))\simeq F(H^n(Q_h(j^*K)))$. They satisfy $F(H^n(\operatorname{counit}_j(K)))=r\circ H^n(\varepsilon_P)\circ l$. Here $Q_h$ includes passage to the homotopy category, $j^*$ is ordinary tensor pullback, and $\operatorname{counit}_j$ is its fixed left-derived comparison [def-pc-standard-single-flat-counit-presentation]. All derived categories are standard [def-pc-derived-category]; stalks are [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. This statement involves no direct image or coefficient module.

proof.text: Bounded-above flatness gives K-flatness; the stalk criterion gives K-flatness of its stalk. Restriction through a ring isomorphism preserves acyclicity and the tensor criterion, so the constructed P remains K-flat.

Apply the derived stalk-extension comparison to j and the given universal pair, transporting the stalk rings along S and V. The resLE composition equation makes the transported ring map the original g.stalkMap. The natural open module-stalk restriction comparison and pinned open-counit compatibility preserve the representative equation. The K-flat scalar-extension counit is invertible on P.

Apply degree-n homology to the derived comparison. Exact stalk homology comparison and the ordinary tensor-stalk formula give the endpoints of l and r. The representative counit equation from the comparison gives their displayed equality; reassociate compositions and cancel inverse localization factors.
